title: Convergent reserve SKU exploration: tiered burst + autoscale pricing
creator: Ava Chen
description: Define and validate a differentiated packaging and pricing approach for Dedicated (reserved GPUs) that combines committed capacity, predictable burst credits, and automated autoscaling lanes across SLA tiers. Aim: create an offer that improves procurement velocity for enterprise buyers, reduces unit cost via smarter autoscale/burst engineering, and simplifies commercial dialogs (quotes, SOWs, security questionnaire responses). This ticket coordinates PM, Sales, Legal, and Engineering to run two parallel experiments (sales pilot + controlled pricing simulation) and deliver contract language, security Q responses, and telemetry to judge success.
objectives: Draft three candidate SKUs that mix committed GPU units, monthly burst credit buckets, and autoscale grace windows
Produce contract clause templates for guaranteed throughput bands, preemption rules, and overage billing
Surface security / compliance answers required for enterprise questionnaires and map to Private offering controls
Instrument telemetry and dashboards to measure economics (unit cost per 1M tokens), utilization, and SLA breach probability
Run a two-week sales pilot with 6 revenue-qualified accounts to validate price sensitivity and packaging clarity
acceptance_criteria: Three SKU proposals with price ladder, example quotes, and margin models for small/medium/large enterprise profiles
Legal-approved contract snippets for burst overage, autoscale billing, and SLA credits
Completed security questionnaire draft for Dedicated + Private controls referencing KMS, audit logs, and network isolation
Telemetry dashboard with: reserved utilization, burst consumption, autoscale events, p95 latency, and SLA credit triggers
Pilot feedback from at least 4 accounts and at least 2 signed letters of intent (LOIs) or firm interest statements
tasks: Kickoff workshop with Sales, Legal, Security, and Eng (completed 2026-03-06)
Model economics: build unit-cost spreadsheet for 12-month reserved vs pay-as-you-go under expected workload shapes
Design SKU matrix: baseline reserved tier + burst credits + autoscale buffer options
Draft contract language and submit to Legal for review
Create security questionnaire answers and map to product controls; run with Security team
Instrument Dedicated runtime telemetry and add Grafana panel mockups
Prepare sales pilot materials: one-pager, sample contract, 3 sample quotes
Run pilot outreach and collect customer interviews
Synthesize pilot learnings and finalize recommended SKU and pricing bands
notes: 2026-03-06: Kickoff held. Attendees: Marcus (PM), Sana (Sales), Omar (Security), Priya (Legal), Diego (Eng). Agreed scope: focus on 3 SKUs and a legal playbook for burst behavior.

2026-03-08: First draft SKU matrix completed. Three approaches: (A) High-commit + small burst; (B) Mid-commit + generous burst + soft autoscale; (C) Low-commit + pay-for-burst pricing. Initial pricing anchored to current Dedicated margins.

2026-03-09: Engineering raised two constraints: autoscale preemption latency (needs kernel-level gating) and billing resolution for sub-minute autoscale events. ENG tickets created to estimate effort (ENG-545210, ENG-545211).
2026-03-11: Security requested explicit wording for KMS key custody and audit log retention durations; drafting answers and mapping to Private offering controls (ongoing).
2026-03-12: Legal suggested adding explicit SLA credit table and a minimum-notice window for burst exhaustion events; updating contract drafts.
2026-03-14: Sales identified six candidate pilot accounts (two startups, three mid-market, one enterprise) and set pilot outreach schedule starting 2026-03-17.

2026-03-15: Pricing sensitivity simulation run across three workload shapes (steady, spiky, seasonal). Preliminary finding: SKU B yields best balance of margin stability and customer appeal for spiky workloads.
Next: finalize pilot pitch materials and ship security questionnaire draft to customer-facing Sales reps by 2026-03-16.
risks: Engineering underestimates autoscale billing complexity leading to delayed rollout
Customers find burst semantics confusing; risk of sales friction and longer procurement cycles
Legal requirements for audit/network isolation extend contract negotiation timelines
Pricing leakage if burst credits are over-generous and not throttled by runtime controls
metrics: MRR uplift from Dedicated packaging: +$75k incremental within first quarter post-launch
